std-agent-context.name: std-agent-context
std-agent-context.description: Wraps llm/token-count + llm/compact — context window management.

std-agent-memory.name: std-agent-memory
std-agent-memory.description: Wraps memory/recall + memory/store — semantic memory for agent loops.

std-agent-session.name: std-agent-session
std-agent-session.description: Wraps session/read-spec + session/write-spec + session/read-history — orbital session data.

std-agent-tool-call.name: std-agent-tool-call
std-agent-tool-call.description: Wraps llm/call-tools — takes messages + tools, returns tool-call result.

std-agent-trace.name: std-agent-trace
std-agent-trace.description: Wraps trace/emit + trace/log — observability for agent loops.

std-agent-fix-loop.name: std-agent-fix-loop
std-agent-fix-loop.description: Agent fix-loop molecule — validate an orbital, generate a repair prompt if errors, apply fix.

std-agent-planner.name: std-agent-planner
std-agent-planner.description: Agent planner molecule — recall memories, then generate a plan from the prompt + recalled context.

std-agent-tool-loop.name: std-agent-tool-loop
std-agent-tool-loop.description: Agent tool-loop molecule — call-tools, check response, emit result for iteration.

std-agent-builder.name: std-agent-builder
std-agent-builder.description: Agent builder organism — plan, build, validate, fix a single orbital end-to-end.

std-agent-rabit.name: std-agent-rabit
std-agent-rabit.description: Rabit organism — coordinator decomposes a prompt into orbital specs, dispatches subagent builds, monitors completion, assembles and validates the composed schema.

std-anim-tick.name: std-anim-tick
std-anim-tick.description: std-anim-tick — sprite animation clock atom. Owns a global animation counter and exposes the current frame NAME (@entity.frameName = frames[counter % len]) every 100ms tick. Boards compose it via `uses` + a trait-ref rebound (linkedEntity) to the board entity; render-ui merges @entity.frameName onto the animated sprite's asset, replacing the inlined animTick frame counters that were duplicated across game boards. 1.1.0 redesign: the 1.0.0 units-frame-advance / effects-aging sets were removed — numeric unit frames served the pre-animation-contract regime (draw-sprite paints atlas sub-texture NAMES, which is exactly what frameName now exposes; zero consumers existed), effects aging is owned by std-fx-particles, and the shared-entity one-writer rule (ORB_SHARED_ENTITY_FIELD_CONFLICT) forbids a shared atom co-writing fields a board's own ticks also write. Tick interval is a language-level literal (100ms); the config surface is `frames`.

std-approval-gate.name: std-approval-gate
std-approval-gate.description: std-approval-gate — generic approval gate / approver workflow. Use when a user voices that an action must be reviewed, approved, signed off, or authorized by a privileged role before it proceeds (admin approval, supervisor sign-off, manager approval, gatekeeper review, editor approval, senior editor approval, reviewer approval, publishing approval, draft approval, content review, submit drafts then editors review and approve or reject, needs approval before going live, requires sign-off before publish). Persists ApprovalRequest rows + surfaces them in a review queue with Approve / Deny / Reject actions, optionally requiring a written rejection reason or feedback comment. On approval emits ApprovalGranted; on denial emits ApprovalDenied. Compose onto any orbital whose action you want to gate: the target orbital emits an external event, an ApprovalRequest row is created, and downstream effects wait on ApprovalGranted. Differs from std-mod-queue, which is content-moderation-specific.

std-audit-capture.name: std-audit-capture
std-audit-capture.description: std-audit-capture — event-interceptor audit log / audit trail. Use when a user voices that a record's changes must be tracked, logged, or auditable (audit trail, track changes, change history, who edited what, mutation log, record changes, log every edit, edit history, modification log, who did what when, accountability log). Listens for the generic `EntityMutated` sentinel (rename via traitOverrides.events to the real mutation event, e.g. ContactSaved) and persists an AuditEntry row capturing actor, action, entity type/id, before/after snapshots, and timestamp. `captureEventTypes` filters on @payload.data.kind (empty = capture all). Compose with `std-lifecycle` to apply retention. Composable via `extraTraits` to interpose audit logging behind any mutating trait.

std-cache-aside.name: std-cache-aside
std-cache-aside.description: infra atom — std-cache-aside (states: cached, empty, error, loading, stale)

std-cascade-on-delete.name: std-cascade-on-delete
std-cascade-on-delete.description: std-cascade-on-delete — relational `owns` cascade. Listens for a parent-deleted sentinel (`ParentDeleted` — rename via traitOverrides.events to the consumer's actual parent-deleted event), then deletes every dependent row whose `foreignKeyField` points at the deleted parent — via a self-driving loop (delete the head of the matching set, re-fetch until none remain). Emits `CascadeRowDeleted` per row and `CascadeCompleted` when done.

std-circuit-breaker.name: std-circuit-breaker
std-circuit-breaker.description: infra atom — std-circuit-breaker (states: closed, halfOpen, open)

std-cooldown.name: std-cooldown
std-cooldown.description: std-cooldown — ability/action cooldown primitive; START begins the countdown, READY fires when it expires.

std-cross-reference.name: std-cross-reference
std-cross-reference.description: std-cross-reference — join-table primitive for N:M relationships. Listens for LinkRequested/UnlinkRequested/FETCH_LINKS_FOR and manages the junction collection (default CrossRefLink [persistent: cross_ref_links]). Rebind via linkedEntity to your consumer junction. Emits LinkCreated, LinkRemoved, LinksLoaded as external broadcasts for downstream consumers.

std-data-erasure.name: std-data-erasure
std-data-erasure.description: std-data-erasure — GDPR Art. 17 right-to-be-forgotten queue. Tracks ErasureRequest rows through pending → grace → executed lifecycle with Cancel during grace. v1.0 ships the request lifecycle UI + knob set; auto-emit of ExecuteErasure after grace lands in v1.1 (loop-with-emit gap — docs/Almadar_Std_Factories.md). Target app/ atoms then own the actual delete or piiFields scrub via an ExecuteErasure listener.

std-game-clock.name: std-game-clock
std-game-clock.description: std-game-clock — fixed-timestep authoritative clock games compose to drive time; emits GameClockTicked every 100ms while running.

std-lifecycle.name: std-lifecycle
std-lifecycle.description: std-lifecycle — age-based status lifecycle for a target entity. A periodic tick scans the target for records in `fromStatus` whose `dateField` is older than `ageDays`, and transitions each one to `toStatus` — every matching record, via a self-driving scan loop (process the head of a filtered fetch, persist the status, re-fetch until the set drains). Compose onto any orbital and bind `targetEntity` + the status/date knobs.

std-migration-job.name: std-migration-job
std-migration-job.description: std-migration-job — one import run of external data into the host system, modeled as a persistent MigrationJob row with a lifecycle state machine: idle → fetching → mapping → reviewing → committing → done | failed. All source access goes through the migration service (call-service "migration" listDocuments / fetchDocument / commit) — the atom never talks to a source directly, and the host-injected service handler resolves credentials from the connectionRef knob (a reference, never the secret). Staging/mapping is host work (deterministic pipeline or agent): the atom fetches, the host stages and emits MIGRATION_STAGED, the user approves (MIGRATION_APPROVED) and only then does commit run. Terminal runs persist the job row for provenance. Rebind the entity to a host-owned job entity via linkedEntity; target and connectionRef are config knobs.
std-migration-job.statePattern: committing, done, failed, fetching, idle, mapping, reviewing

std-mod-queue.name: std-mod-queue
std-mod-queue.description: std-mod-queue — moderation queue for content review. Owns a ModQueueItem entity (one row per flagged target) and a single review trait that loads pending items, renders them in a data-grid with Approve / Reject / Escalate actions, and persists the reviewer's verdict back to the row.

std-notify-on-event.name: std-notify-on-event
std-notify-on-event.description: std-notify-on-event — cross-orbital wiring atom. Subscribes to events from another orbital (e.g. CheckoutOrbital emits OrderPlaced, OrderRecordOrbital reacts via this atom) and dispatches a notification. Use when one orbital needs to react to or be notified about events that happen in another orbital — the wiring goes through this atom's `EventOccurred` listener which the molecule renames via traitOverrides.events to the upstream event name. Resolves recipient from `recipients` (first entry; multi-recipient fan-out is a future extension) or falls back to `@user.id`. Skips dispatch when the recipient is in `suppressionList`. Emits in-app `notify` when `notifyChannel` is `"in-app"`, or persists a `NotificationRecord` row for out-of-band delivery when channel is `"email"` or `"sms"`.

std-reminder-scheduler.name: std-reminder-scheduler
std-reminder-scheduler.description: std-reminder-scheduler — deadline reminders for a target entity. A periodic tick scans the target for records whose `dateField` deadline is within `offsetHours` of now and that have not been reminded yet, and emits `ReminderDue` for each — every matching record, via a self-driving scan loop. Marks each record `remindedAt` so it isn't reminded twice. Compose alongside std-notify-on-event to deliver the reminder.

std-row-access-control.name: std-row-access-control
std-row-access-control.description: std-row-access-control — row-level access control gate / ownership filter / role-based row visibility. Use when a user voices that only certain users should see or edit certain records (only the owner can edit, private to owner, owner-only visibility, only see your own records, role-based visibility, admin-only access, visible to admins only, restricted to role, permission gate, ownership scoping, hide from other users, only show mine). Listens for `RowsLoaded` (rename via traitOverrides.events to the consumer's load event), filters `@payload.data` by `@user.id` (when `ownerField` is set) and/or `@user.role` (when `visibleRoles` is non-empty), re-emits `RowsFiltered` for downstream consumers (rename to wire into the UI atom's listen). Composable via `extraTraits` to interpose between a data fetch and a list/grid UI.

std-status-lifecycle.name: std-status-lifecycle
std-status-lifecycle.description: Infra substrate: data-driven entity status lifecycle. The statuses and the allowed transitions are config data over a fixed single-state topology, so a host organism can expand or collapse its lifecycle without forking. Compose onto an entity, rename the ChangeStatusRequested listen to the host's status-change action, and supply `states` + `transitions`. A requested move is validated against the `transitions` table (illegal moves are rejected), then the new value is written to `statusField` on the target entity and StatusChanged is emitted. Surfaces nothing — the host renders the badge and buttons.

std-status-lifecycle-control.name: std-status-lifecycle-control
std-status-lifecycle-control.description: Status lifecycle control — infra molecule pairing std-status-lifecycle's StatusMachine, which deliberately surfaces no UI of its own. Pure presentational: shows the current status and one button per legal next move (config.transitions filtered on config.currentStatus), emitting ChangeStatusRequested with the picked move's id/from/to on click. Driven entirely by config (currentStatus/recordId/transitions) rather than a bound entity, so a host embeds it inline at the record it's viewing (currentStatus={@entity.status} recordId={@entity.id} transitions matching the paired StatusMachine's own config.transitions) and points that StatusMachine's `listens` at this trait's emit (`<Composer>.ChangeStatusRequested -> ChangeStatusRequested`) instead of at a dead declared-only event.

std-data-collector.name: std-data-collector
std-data-collector.description: std-data-collector — pure buffer-accumulation atom, parameterized for any ML domain. Collects data points into a buffer and fires BUFFER_READY with the full accumulated buffer once it reaches config.bufferSize, then resets for the next cycle. No ML compute, no model call — state machine + array operators only. Use ahead of a training loop, a batch inference call, or any downstream rung that needs a fixed-size window of accumulated observations.

std-graph-builder.name: std-graph-builder
std-graph-builder.description: Graph construction atom — builds node/edge structures from an entity collection for downstream GNN pipelines; pure array/object transform, no ML compute.

std-ml-classify.name: std-ml-classify
std-ml-classify.description: Generative rung (R5) — structured LLM verdict from a closed category set, via the llm.classify service seam. Bottom of the fall-through: always answers or fails, never abstains.

std-ml-exact-check.name: std-ml-exact-check
std-ml-exact-check.description: Rung R0 of the intelligence ladder — normalizes and compares a candidate value against a key value; abstains on no match.

std-ml-infer.name: std-ml-infer
std-ml-infer.description: std-ml-infer — the learned rung (R4) of the intelligence ladder, and the seam between a .lolo circuit and a trained model deployed on masar (or off-the-shelf HuggingFace weights) reached through the ml service. Sends the caller-supplied input straight to call-service ml infer, then guards the raw output before it ever becomes an effect: validates it against the declared outputContract, clamps it into range, and only then decides. Emits INFERRED when the output satisfies the contract and confidence clears confidenceFloor — carrying the clamped output, confidence, and an empty violations list. Otherwise abstains with INFER_ABSTAINED, whose reason is one of: low confidence (contract satisfied but below floor, violations empty), contract violation (violations populated via contract/violations for diagnosis), or unavailable (the service call itself failed — a masar cold start or a down endpoint, never surfaced as a user-visible error). Use when a numeric or tensor-shaped model answer needs a licensed guard before becoming a decision — classification scores, regressions, embedding-derived predictions — and the next rung (R5 generative) should take over on any abstain.

std-ml-label-capture.name: std-ml-label-capture
std-ml-label-capture.description: std-ml-label-capture — records a labeled example (input, verdict, source rung, observed outcome) so that expensive top-rung answers become training data for a cheaper rung later. Generic: it knows nothing about grading or students. sampleRate gates what fraction of examples are kept (1 = capture all); sink tags which named destination the example is attributed to.

std-ml-lookup.name: std-ml-lookup
std-ml-lookup.description: Rung R1 of the intelligence ladder — finds the candidate value in a list of accepted values; abstains when nothing matches.

std-ml-posterior.name: std-ml-posterior
std-ml-posterior.description: std-ml-posterior — the statistical rung (R2) of the intelligence ladder. Holds a Beta(alpha, beta) belief over an unknown success rate and updates it from boolean observations (Bayesian updating, knowledge tracing, Thompson-sampling prior). After each observation it draws samples from the posterior, computes a credible interval, and decides: MASTERY_REACHED when the mean clears the floor with a tight interval, REMEDIATION_NEEDED when the mean sits at or below the ceiling with the same confidence, or EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT — the abstain — when the interval is still too wide to trust. Use when a hand-tuned score needs to become a belief that can say 'not enough evidence yet' (mastery, skill, risk, preference, difficulty).

std-ml-similarity.name: std-ml-similarity
std-ml-similarity.description: Retrieval rung (R3) — embed a candidate against references and gate on cosine floor + margin; abstains when not confident.

std-tokenizer.name: std-tokenizer
std-tokenizer.description: std-tokenizer — a text-preprocessing atom for tokenization. Splits raw text into a token sequence using a configurable method (whitespace, character, or arbitrary delimiter), normalizes and truncates the sequence, then maps each token to a vocabulary id (falling back to unkId when the token is absent from config.vocab). Feeds downstream embedding or sequence-model atoms. Pure circuit logic: str/* and array/* operators only, no ML compute, no model call.

std-weight-validator.name: std-weight-validator
std-weight-validator.description: std-weight-validator — a constraint-checking atom for model weights, applying the same discipline as the zero-warning validator to weights: constrained and checked, not trusted (Almadar_Intelligence_Ladder.md §7.5). Checks a candidate weight tensor against three pure predicate constraints — magnitude bounds (every element's absolute value must clear maxMagnitude), forbidden regions (excluded [min,max] bands no weight may land in even within the magnitude bound), and a regression threshold against a baseline tensor (per-element drift must not exceed regressionThreshold; 0 disables the check) — and reports every violated check with its detail. Emits WEIGHTS_ACCEPTED when all three checks clear, or WEIGHTS_REJECTED carrying the full violations list otherwise. Pure circuit logic: predicates and comparisons only, no ML compute, no model call.

std-escalating-decision.name: std-escalating-decision
std-escalating-decision.description: std-escalating-decision — the intelligence ladder itself, as one reusable composition. One request enters at DECIDE and falls through the rungs in order — R0 exact check, R1 table lookup, R3 retrieval, R4 learned inference, R5 generative classification — each rung handing off to the next by abstaining, until one proves the answer. Exits DECIDED, tagged with which rung answered (rung, confidence, matched, reasoning), or DECISION_FAILED if even the generative floor could not serve it. The escalation is a chain, not a hub: each rung listens directly to the rung above it and projects its own inputs out of the carried request, so the trait graph is a DAG and no event ever returns to a rung that already ran. Domain-agnostic: it knows about candidates and categories, not students or quizzes — grading, routing, matching, moderation, and duplicate detection are all this same molecule with different knobs. R2 (the Beta posterior) is deliberately not in this chain: it is the 'decide what to do next' half of a turn and already lives in std-knowledge-tracing.

std-knowledge-tracing.name: std-knowledge-tracing
std-knowledge-tracing.description: std-knowledge-tracing — turns one true/false observation ('did the learner get this right?') into a tracked belief about mastery, and captures the same observation as a labeled training example in the same motion. Composes std-ml-posterior (the R2 statistical rung — a Beta-Bernoulli belief over an unknown success rate) with std-ml-label-capture: every posterior verdict — MASTERY_REACHED, REMEDIATION_NEEDED, or the abstain EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT — becomes a persisted labeled example (the input skill, the posterior's own verdict, and the ground-truth outcome that produced it), so a cheaper rung can later be trained to reproduce the same call without running the statistics. Domain-agnostic: it knows about skills and observations, not students, quizzes, or courses. One instance tracks one belief (e.g. one learner × one skill); the host composes as many instances as it has beliefs to hold.

ui-behavior-view.name: ui-behavior-view
ui-behavior-view.description: BehaviorView — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui behavior-view pattern).

ui-module-card.name: ui-module-card
ui-module-card.description: ModuleCard — a card summarizing one course module or lesson with progress and entry point. — UI factory (1:1 with the @almadar/ui module-card pattern).
ui-module-card.capabilities: course module card, lesson card, curriculum unit card, learning-path step card

std-app-layout.name: std-app-layout
std-app-layout.description: std-app-layout — dashboard-layout chrome (sidebar nav + top bar with search + topBarActions + notifications) wrapping a single contentTrait slot. Use for list-style apps (CMS / helpdesk / CRM) and account/settings pages: the chrome stays stable while the consumer's content trait renders the data, and the consumer can add domain icons (cart / profile / help) via topBarActions. Bind once per orbital — the consumer rebinds linkedEntity via `XAppLayout = AppShell.traits.AppLayout -> XEntity` so multiple orbitals in one file each get their own chrome without colliding on a shared atom entity.
std-app-layout.capabilities: settings page shell, preferences page, account settings layout, profile settings, admin console shell

std-app-search.name: std-app-search
std-app-search.description: std-app-search — reusable global search: wraps a host content view and, on a SEARCH trigger, fetches the linked entity filtered by @config.searchField and renders the matching results, then CLEAR_SEARCH returns to the host view. Rebind to any entity; point @config.idleContent at the normal view and wire a trigger (e.g. AppLayout SEARCH) into SEARCH.

std-billable-hour.name: std-billable-hour
std-billable-hour.description: std-billable-hour — generic billable-hour timesheet primitive for legal, agency, and consulting domains. Lists entries in `browsing`; opens entry detail in `viewing_single` with Invoice / Write Off actions.

std-board.name: std-board
std-board.description: std-board — generic N-column board primitive. `config.columns` is an array of column definitions ({ key, label, icon, variant }); the trait `array/map`s them on `BoardItemsLoaded` into `@entity.boards` where each board carries its filtered items + a count. The render is a `data-grid` over `@entity.boards` (one card per column) whose `renderItem` lambda nests a `data-list` over `@col.items` (the cards in that stage). N is config-driven — pass any number of columns; the outer `data-grid`'s `cols` is bound to `@config.gridCols` so the grid wraps if you exceed it. Topology = loading / viewing_board / viewing_card / adding / error — distinct from the cookie-cutter `loading/browsing/viewing_single/error` CRUD shape. App-level atoms (e.g. std-pipeline) compose std-board via `uses` and add a sibling persistor + extended source entity. `config.boardLook` switches the board body between the default N-column grid ('columns') and a Trello-style wide-column kanban ('kanban-classic').

std-browse.name: std-browse
std-browse.description: std-browse as a Function — single primitive: data-grid. Owns the fetch + REFETCH (query/filter/page) state machine. Consumers configure fields/imageField/itemActions/cols/gap/variant; the atom renders the grid. Each `fields[]` entry accepts `{ name, label, variant }` plus optional `referenceEntity` + `displayField` to render a foreign-key column as the joined entity's display value (data-grid resolves @list[referenceEntity] at render time when both keys are present). `browseLook` (table default / dense / feed / gallery / master-detail / triage) selects one of six render bodies; dense/feed/gallery were folded in from std-browse-dense/-feed/-gallery (Phase 5.B); master-detail (split record view driven by the guarded VIEW/CLOSE self-transitions) and triage (inbox rows) were folded in 2026-07-26. Consumers retarget by setting browseLook.

std-calendar.name: std-calendar
std-calendar.description: std-calendar as a Function — owns the fetch + SELECT_DAY state machine; default bodyContent renders the month-grid + upcoming-events tree. `config.calendarLook` switches the body between the default month-grid ('month'), a day-grouped agenda list ('agenda-list'), and a 7-column week timeline ('week-timeline') while inheriting the same trait, state machine, emits, and listens.

std-confirmation.name: std-confirmation
std-confirmation.description: Modal-only confirmation trait: renders ONLY to the `modal` slot. Consumers configure icon/title/alertMessage/confirmLabel at the trait-ref call site via `config: { ... }`. Side effects (persist delete, notify, etc.) belong in a sibling coordinator trait that `listens { ConfirmTrait CONFIRM -> DO_DELETE }`.

std-dashboard-grid-embedded.name: std-dashboard-grid-embedded
std-dashboard-grid-embedded.description: std-dashboard-grid-embedded — embeddable sibling of std-dashboard-grid-layout. Renders the same toolbar / filter / 12-tile grid contract WITHOUT wrapping it in dashboard-layout chrome (no sidebar, no appName, no nav). Use inside another app shell that already owns the surrounding chrome.

std-date-range.name: std-date-range
std-date-range.description: std-date-range — compact calendar button (Looker / Tableau shape) that opens a popover containing the date-range-picker. Owns a DateRange runtime entity; DATE_RANGE_CHANGED persists @payload.from + @payload.to so cross-trait listeners can route the range into data atoms (Browse REFETCH_FILTER, Stats / Graphs requery).

std-esign-flow.name: std-esign-flow
std-esign-flow.description: std-esign-flow — the send-for-signature flow: list signature requests, create one (pick document + recipient), resend or cancel, track status. Composes std-file-store + std-esign-request; no document-rendering or code-preview chrome.

std-esign-request.name: std-esign-request
std-esign-request.description: std-esign-request — specialized e-signature request tracker: send a document out for signing and track its status (draft/sent/viewed/signed/declined/expired). Just the request list + send/revoke; signature capture is std-signature-capture's job.

std-event-log.name: std-event-log
std-event-log.description: std-event-log — generic chronological event feed (Stripe activity log / GitHub PR timeline / Linear event feed style). Renders a vertical `timeline` with type-coded dots, a single horizontal chip-bar of kind filters (All + per-kind), reverse-chronological sort, and an inline form for logging events that weren't auto-captured. `config.kindOptions` maps each kind → status/icon/label so consuming molecules/organisms get type-coded visuals without re-implementing topology. Topology = loading / viewing / backfilling / error.

std-export.name: std-export
std-export.description: std-export — a dropdown format menu (CSV/XLSX/PDF defaults; caller can override via config.formats). Emits EXPORT_REQUESTED { itemId, label } on the bus — itemId is the picked format id; host or sibling orbital generates the file. A format entry may carry `url`: the menu then downloads that file directly on pick (gesture-driven; the event still emits) — used for pre-baked artifacts like sprite sheets. tileId is a static per-instance config value, not echoed in the click payload.

std-file-store.name: std-file-store
std-file-store.description: std-file-store — the generic file/page tree primitive. A file-tree + config-driven data table over a hierarchical collection; opens a row in `viewing_single` with config-driven detail actions. Rebindable: pass `fields`/`itemActions`/`detailActions`/`tree` to retarget it at any hierarchical entity (files, wiki pages, note trees). Folds in the former std-page-tree via `reorderable` + a page field/action set.

std-filter.name: std-filter
std-filter.description: std-filter — single primitive: filter-group. Owns a FilterTarget runtime entity; every FILTER transition persists field/value so cross-trait listeners can route the latest selection into data atoms.

std-form-advanced.name: std-form-advanced
std-form-advanced.description: std-form-advanced — full-typed form-section primitive. Hosts the `editing` state with a configurable `fields` array (each entry mirrors @almadar/ui's `form-section` field schema: `{ name, label, type?, values?, relation?, required? }`). Field-level constraints live in `config.fieldValidation` as `[{ field, format?: 'email'|'url'|'phone', regex?, minLength?, maxLength?, message? }]` — form-section surfaces inline errors when a submit violates a declared constraint. Agents drive shape by overriding `config.fields` + `config.fieldValidation` per-call-site.

std-gallery.name: std-gallery
std-gallery.description: std-gallery — image gallery primitive. Browses GalleryItems in a media-gallery grid; opens a lightbox modal for full-size viewing.

std-geosearch.name: std-geosearch
std-geosearch.description: std-geosearch — location-aware search variant: search-input + map-view + range-slider for radius. Owns a GeoSearchResult runtime entity; GEO_SEARCH persists @payload.searchTerm/lat/lng/radiusKm so cross-trait listeners can route them into geo-aware data atoms.

std-graphs.name: std-graphs
std-graphs.description: std-graphs — embeddable chart atom. ITEMS_LOADED groups @payload.data by @config.categoryField (or @config.timeField when timeAxis=true) and aggregates per bucket. Multi-series rendering via @config.series (preformatted ChartSeries shape). Histograms via chartType=histogram pass pre-binned @payload.data through unchanged. Stacked / 100% stacked bars via @config.stack. Post-process sort + limit. Clicking a data point emits UI:@config.drillEvent with { label, value, seriesLabel? }. Drop into a dashboard alongside std-stats / std-browse.

std-image-upload-multi.name: std-image-upload-multi
std-image-upload-multi.description: std-image-upload-multi — multi-image upload with drop zone, gallery preview, and per-batch progress.

std-import.name: std-import
std-import.description: std-import — a dropdown source menu (Paste text / Markdown files defaults; caller can override via config.sources) plus the OS file picker for file-kind sources. Emits IMPORT_REQUESTED { source, files } on the bus — source is the picked SourceOption descriptor; files carries file metadata when the picker ran (empty otherwise). The actual import work is delegated to a sibling std-migration-job, which listens for IMPORT_REQUESTED and drives the migration service. Mirrors std-export: the menu emits each entry's own literal event field, so overriding the event alone does not retarget the click — also set sources[].event to match.

std-list.name: std-list
std-list.description: Daisy-chain composition showcase: no `on EVENT { ... }` trait-ref overrides. Modal + Confirmation trait refs are configured via `config: { ... }` at the call site. Side effects (persist) live in a sibling coordinator trait (`ListItemPersistor`) that listens for the modal/confirmation trait emits. Mirrors std-cart's structure. std-list omits the read-only VIEW path that the old version had — form-section's mode set only supports "create" | "edit", and a dedicated detail-view pattern is tracked separately (std-detail).

std-modal.name: std-modal
std-modal.description: Modal-only trait: renders ONLY to the `modal` slot. The parent molecule's layout/browse trait is responsible for the `main` slot (the list, the trigger buttons, etc.). Consumers configure icon/title/fields/mode at the trait-ref call site via `config: { ... }`. Side effects (persist, notify) belong in a sibling coordinator trait that `listens { ModalTrait SAVE -> DO_PERSIST }`.

std-multi-party-flow.name: std-multi-party-flow
std-multi-party-flow.description: std-multi-party-flow — Escrow.com / DocuSign / Stripe Connect style multi-party transaction. Header + summary (subject/amount/reference) + named parties (avatar/role/actor) + stage progress + your-turn panel + activity feed + dispute/cancel escape hatches. Topology = loading / awaiting / capturing_dispute / capturing_cancel / funded / released / disputed / cancelled / error.
std-multi-party-flow.statePattern: awaiting, cancelled, capturing_cancel, capturing_dispute, disputed, error, funded, loading, released

std-notification-panel.name: std-notification-panel
std-notification-panel.description: std-notification-panel — the bell's overlay surface. A dedicated modal-only trait that renders the notification list a consumer already passes to std-app-layout's `notifications` knob, and dismisses with a single (render-ui modal null). Mount it beside the app layout and route the layout's notificationClickEvent into OPEN; the catalog trait underneath is never repainted, so opening and closing the bell cannot strand the viewer. Owning the overlay in its own trait is what makes the shape legal — a modal rendered from the trait that also owns `main` is rejected by CIRCUIT_MODAL_EXIT_INCOMPLETE.
std-notification-panel.capabilities: notification overlay, alerts panel, bell dropdown, notification centre, inbox overlay

std-pagination.name: std-pagination
std-pagination.description: std-pagination — single primitive: pagination control. PAGE accepts the Pagination component's `{page}` emit; ITEMS_LOADED accepts an upstream `{data:[ObjectSpec]}` payload and derives totalPages = ceil(len/pageSize). Molecules wire `BrowseItemLoaded -> ITEMS_LOADED` to keep it in lockstep with the data hub.

std-rating-review.name: std-rating-review
std-rating-review.description: std-rating-review — Airbnb / Amazon / Google Maps style review surface. Header with aggregate score + Write CTA, per-star distribution bars, working sort chips (recent / top rated / lowest), scrollable reviews list with author + stars + comment + helpful action. Topology = loading / viewing / composing / submitting / submitted / error.
std-rating-review.statePattern: composing, error, loading, submitted, submitting, viewing

std-recurrence.name: std-recurrence
std-recurrence.description: std-recurrence — recurring-rule definition + upcoming runs (Stripe Subscriptions / Cron Hub style). The viewing state shows a plain-English rule sentence and the next N dated runs as an agenda timeline. Per-run exception modal supports skip / reschedule. Topology = loading / defining_rule / viewing / awaiting_exception_decision / cancelled / error.
std-recurrence.statePattern: awaiting_exception_decision, cancelled, defining_rule, error, loading, viewing

std-related.name: std-related
std-related.description: Relation-rendering atom. Assumes the linked entity's relation field has already been hydrated by an upstream fetch with include; this atom only owns the rendering of the related children. Paired with std-browse via @trait.X this gives a one-line master-detail layout: hstack [ @trait.ParentList, @trait.ParentRelated ]. The molecule std-related-master-detail is the canonical showcase.

std-rich-editor.name: std-rich-editor
std-rich-editor.description: std-rich-editor — wiki/CMS Notion-style block editor. Browses documents in `browsing`; opens the rich-block-editor on a selected row; persists block edits + publish status.
std-rich-editor.capabilities: notes app, note-taking, journal, personal journal entries, document editor, write and organize notes

std-saved-search.name: std-saved-search
std-saved-search.description: std-saved-search — persisted query + alert subscription. Owns a SavedSearch entity (one row per saved query) and a single manage trait that lists saved searches in a data-grid, lets users toggle their alert subscription / rename the search / delete it, and persists each change.

std-scatter.name: std-scatter
std-scatter.description: std-scatter — embeddable scatter / bubble chart atom. ITEMS_LOADED maps @payload.data into {x,y,label,size,color} points using configured fields (no aggregation step — distinct from std-graphs). Drop into a dashboard alongside std-stats / std-graphs for two-numeric correlation views.

std-search.name: std-search

std-selection.name: std-selection

std-signature-capture.name: std-signature-capture
std-signature-capture.description: std-signature-capture — a drawn-signature pad. The signer draws, clears, or submits; on submit the signature persists and the atom emits SignatureSubmitted. One job: capture a signature and report when done.

std-stats.name: std-stats
std-stats.description: std-stats — embeddable analytics-card atom. ITEMS_LOADED aggregates @payload.data per @config.metrics (count|sum|avg|min|max|variance with optional filter, baselineFilter, format, icon, max, target, trend, trendPolarity, sparkline) and renders one stat-display per entry. Variance metrics compute actual - baseline using `filter` + `baselineFilter` lambdas and report the signed delta as trend. clickEvent emits UI:{clickEvent} { metricLabel } when a card is clicked. Drop into a dashboard alongside std-browse / std-search / std-filter. `config.statsLook` switches the whole body between the default per-metric card grid ('cards'), a Stripe-dashboard KPI tile row ('kpi-tiles'), a single hero metric card ('hero-metric'), and a chart-first sparkline tile grid ('sparkline-row').

std-step-flow.name: std-step-flow
std-step-flow.description: std-step-flow — generic N-step sequential decision chain (Stripe Connect / TurboTax / Vercel deploy style). `config.steps` is an array of step definitions `{ key, label, description, icon, allowedRoles?: [string] }`; the trait projects the current step into a prominent body card and a `wizard-progress` stepper bar at the top. When a step declares `allowedRoles`, only users whose `@user.role` is in that list can advance through it. One primary button ADVANCEs along the chain; at the last step the same button finalizes (label/icon/variant swap via entity binding, state routed via guard). REJECT/ESCALATE terminate. Topology = loading / running / approved / rejected / escalated / error.
std-step-flow.statePattern: approved, error, escalated, loading, rejected, running

std-tabs.name: std-tabs

std-tag-taxonomy.name: std-tag-taxonomy
std-tag-taxonomy.description: std-tag-taxonomy — hierarchical category tag tree (parent/child). TagBrowse fetches Tag rows on INIT, renders the active level via data-grid, and on SELECT_TAG drills into a tag's children by binding @entity.id to the chosen parent.

std-thread.name: std-thread
std-thread.description: std-thread — forum-style nested replies with collapse + flat-mode toggle. Owns ThreadPost (persistent). flat:true covers 1:1 linear inquiry threads; flat:false renders forum-style nested. INIT fetches; REPLY persists a child post under @payload.parentId. Layer 3 variants override `bodyContent` to deliver chat-bubble, email-threaded, or linear-comments UX while inheriting the same trait, state machine, emits, and listens.

std-version-history.name: std-version-history
std-version-history.description: std-version-history — wiki/CMS revision history with diff + rollback. Browses revisions; opens detail in `viewing_single`; compares two revisions in `comparing` with intrinsic version-diff; persists rollback.

std-vote.name: std-vote
std-vote.description: std-vote — forum-style up/down vote tally with single-vote-per-user constraint. Owns a Vote entity; VOTE persists the new direction (toggling to none when re-clicking the active arrow) and emits VoteCasted so cross-trait listeners can recompute aggregates.

std-wizard.name: std-wizard
std-wizard.description: std-wizard — generic N-step data-collection wizard (Vercel deploy / GitHub repo create / Stripe Connect onboarding style). Each step has its own form fields. Topology = loading / running / completed / cancelled / error. ADVANCE is guard-routed: not-last-step advances; last-step transitions to completed. Distinct from std-step-flow (approval-decision) — wizard collects data via form-section per step, step-flow collects yes/no decisions.

std-arcade-flow.name: std-arcade-flow
std-arcade-flow.description: Headless win/lose authority for the arcade play-for-tickets loop: owns only result. Listens SCORE_CHANGED (tickets + tokens) and sets result to won once tickets reach the target, lost when tokens run out first, else none. Renders nothing.

std-arcade-play.name: std-arcade-play
std-arcade-play.description: Headless arcade play-economy mechanic: the SOLE writer of tokens + tickets + machines. Applies a PLAY_MACHINE intent (spends a token, rolls a pseudo-random ticket payout within a configured range, emits BURST + SCORE_CHANGED). Renders nothing.

std-chase-ai.name: std-chase-ai
std-chase-ai.description: Headless chase-AI mechanic: enemies damage adjacent targets, else step toward the nearest target respecting tile passability and occupancy.

std-dungeon-combat.name: std-dungeon-combat
std-dungeon-combat.description: Headless dungeon combat authority: owns the enemy roster, hero HP, and kill score. Bump-attacks damage enemies; monster ticks chase the hero and deal contact damage.

std-fx-particles.name: std-fx-particles
std-fx-particles.description: Headless floating-text/particle mechanic: decays each fx entry's ttl every tick and drops the dead ones, and appends spawned particles on BURST. Composed onto a [runtime, shared] game entity; renders nothing (the board owns the single render authority).

std-gather.name: std-gather
std-gather.description: Headless resource-gathering mechanic: owns features + wood + stone. Listens HERO_STEPPED and, when the hero lands on a wood/stone-type feature, increments the matching resource, removes the node, emits a BURST pickup particle, and emits RESOURCES so survival-flow can decide loss. Never writes units.

std-gold.name: std-gold
std-gold.description: Headless gold-economy mechanic: the SOLE writer of gold. Listens a mine-hit signal and adds a fixed yield; emits GOLD_CHANGED. Renders nothing.

std-grid-tactics.name: std-grid-tactics
std-grid-tactics.description: Headless grid-tactics unit-authority: the SOLE writer of units. Applies MOVE/ATTACK/SPAWN/HEAL intents from any source (player, AI, production, or progression) and runs the enemy AI_TURN pipeline, emitting BURST hit-particles and UNITS_CHANGED survivor counts. Renders nothing.

std-hero-nav.name: std-hero-nav
std-hero-nav.description: Headless single-hero navigation authority: the SOLE writer of units + movesLeft on objective boards. Applies a budget-limited MOVE intent (steps the hero one tile, spends a move, emits HERO_STEPPED) and an optional WANDER intent (random step for neutral NPCs). Renders nothing.

std-market-flow.name: std-market-flow
std-market-flow.description: Headless win/lose authority for market-service boards: owns only result. Listens SERVICE_CHANGED (served + lost) and sets result to won when enough customers are served, lost when too many patience timers expire, else none. Renders nothing.

std-mesh-asset-art.name: std-mesh-asset-art
std-mesh-asset-art.description: MeshAssetArtCollector — SOLE writer of @entity.meshAssetArt: collects volumetric asset catalogs published on the bus (MESH_ASSET_PUBLISH { kind, states }) into one kind → (state → draw-group items of draw-mesh descriptors) map that 3D board frames select per-row per anim state. INIT seeds from config and emits MESH_ASSET_SYNC so already-mounted catalogs republish regardless of mount order; the SYNC self-hop re-applies the seed after sibling canvas stashes exist (Almadar_Runtime_Gaps.md R-INIT-SEED-REPAINT-RACE). The 3D twin of SvgAssetArtCollector. Renders nothing — render authority stays with the frame.

std-objective-flow.name: std-objective-flow
std-objective-flow.description: Headless win/lose authority for objective boards: owns only result. Listens PROGRESS (objectivesLeft + movesLeft) and sets result to won when every objective is reached, lost when the move budget runs out first, else none. Renders nothing.

std-objective-reach.name: std-objective-reach
std-objective-reach.description: Headless reach-the-objective mechanic: owns features + score + objectivesLeft. Listens HERO_STEPPED and, when the hero lands on a target-type feature, scores it (optionally removing the model), emits a BURST pickup particle, and emits PROGRESS so round-flow can decide win/lose. Never writes units.

std-patience.name: std-patience
std-patience.description: Headless customer-service mechanic: owns a stationary customer roster with per-customer patience. Decrements patience every tick, serves nearby customers on HERO_STEPPED (resets their patience + scores), and emits CUSTOMER_LOST when a timer expires. Never writes units.

std-production.name: std-production
std-production.description: Headless unit-production mechanic: accrues productionPoints each turn (AI_TURN) and, on an affordable PRODUCE, emits a SPAWN intent for the grid-tactics authority to place a new unit. Owns only productionPoints (+ its spawn counter); never writes units directly.

std-round-flow.name: std-round-flow
std-round-flow.description: Headless win/lose round-resolution mechanic: derives result (victory/defeat/none) from team survivor counts on each UNITS_CHANGED signal and emits GAME_END. Owns only result; boards own their own phase/turn. Renders nothing.

std-score.name: std-score
std-score.description: Headless scoring mechanic: awards points when the enemy survivor count drops on a UNITS_CHANGED signal. Owns only score (+ its kill baseline); renders nothing.

std-survival-flow.name: std-survival-flow
std-survival-flow.description: Headless win/lose authority for the nature-survival board: owns only result. Listens RESOURCES (movesLeft) and sets result to lost when the move budget runs out before the camp is built; listens BUILD_CAMP (the render-gated win intent) and sets result to won. Renders nothing.

std-svg-asset-art.name: std-svg-asset-art
std-svg-asset-art.description: SvgAssetArtCollector — SOLE writer of @entity.svgAssetArt: collects vector asset catalogs published on the bus (SVG_ASSET_PUBLISH { kind, states }) into one kind → (state → draw-group items) map that board frames select per-row per anim state. INIT seeds from config and emits SVG_ASSET_SYNC so already-mounted catalogs republish regardless of mount order; the SYNC self-hop re-applies the seed after sibling canvas stashes exist (Almadar_Runtime_Gaps.md R-INIT-SEED-REPAINT-RACE). Renders nothing — render authority stays with the frame.

std-xp.name: std-xp
std-xp.description: Headless XP/progression mechanic: grants xp when the enemy survivor count drops (UNITS_CHANGED), and on reaching xpToNext levels up — raising the threshold and emitting a HEAL reward the grid-tactics authority applies. Owns only xp/xpToNext/level (+ kill baseline); never writes units.

std-algo-astargraph.name: std-algo-astargraph
std-algo-astargraph.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): A* engine — each tick expands the min-f (g+straight-line-h) node toward the goal on the weighted biology-canvas.

std-algo-astargrid.name: std-algo-astargrid
std-algo-astargrid.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): A* shortest path on a walled grid — each tick expands the open cell of least f=g+h, Manhattan heuristic, on cells.

std-algo-bfs.name: std-algo-bfs
std-algo-bfs.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Breadth-first search engine — dequeues one node per tick, enqueues its unseen neighbours, recolours the graph on biology-canvas.

std-algo-binarysearch.name: std-algo-binarysearch
std-algo-binarysearch.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Binary-search engine — one lo/hi/mid narrowing step per tick over a sorted bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed via `uses`.

std-algo-bubblesort.name: std-algo-bubblesort
std-algo-bubblesort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Bubble-sort engine — one adjacent compare/swap per tick over a bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`.

std-algo-dfs.name: std-algo-dfs
std-algo-dfs.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Depth-first search engine — pops one node per tick off a LIFO stack, pushes its unseen neighbours, recolours the graph on biology-canvas.

std-algo-dijkstra.name: std-algo-dijkstra
std-algo-dijkstra.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Dijkstra engine — each tick settles the nearest unvisited node and relaxes its weighted edges on biology-canvas.

std-algo-floodfill.name: std-algo-floodfill
std-algo-floodfill.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Flood fill — each tick dequeues one cell, recolours it, and enqueues its 4-neighbours sharing the seed's value on algorithm-canvas cells.

std-algo-gameoflife.name: std-algo-gameoflife
std-algo-gameoflife.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Conway's Game of Life — each tick recomputes every cell's next state from its eight neighbours, on algorithm-canvas cells.

std-algo-gridbfs.name: std-algo-gridbfs
std-algo-gridbfs.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Grid BFS wavefront — each tick dequeues one open cell and enqueues its non-wall 4-neighbours, expanding toward the target on algorithm-canvas cells.

std-algo-heapsort.name: std-algo-heapsort
std-algo-heapsort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Heapsort engine — one sift-down compare/swap or extract-max micro-step per tick over a bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`.

std-algo-insertionsort.name: std-algo-insertionsort
std-algo-insertionsort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Insertion-sort engine — one shift/settle step per tick over a bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`.

std-algo-mazegen.name: std-algo-mazegen
std-algo-mazegen.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Randomized-DFS maze carving — each tick carves to a random unvisited room two cells away or backtracks, on cells.

std-algo-mergesort.name: std-algo-mergesort
std-algo-mergesort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Bottom-up mergesort engine — one merged element copied per tick from an aux snapshot over a bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`.

std-algo-mst.name: std-algo-mst
std-algo-mst.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Prim minimum-spanning-tree engine — each tick adds the lightest edge crossing the tree cut on biology-canvas.

std-algo-quicksort.name: std-algo-quicksort
std-algo-quicksort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Iterative quicksort engine — one Lomuto micro-step per tick over a bar array on algorithm-canvas, driven by an explicit range stack; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`.

std-algo-selectionsort.name: std-algo-selectionsort
std-algo-selectionsort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Selection-sort engine — one scan-compare or swap step per tick over a bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`.

std-algo-slidingwindow.name: std-algo-slidingwindow
std-algo-slidingwindow.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Sliding-window engine — one fixed-size window slide per tick tracking the max-sum window on algorithm-canvas; composed via `uses`.

std-algo-toposort.name: std-algo-toposort
std-algo-toposort.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Topological sort engine (Kahn) — each tick emits the first node whose predecessors are all ordered, recolours the DAG on biology-canvas.

std-algo-twopointer.name: std-algo-twopointer
std-algo-twopointer.description: Algorithm-animation engine (algorithm-canvas): Two-pointer engine — one left/right pair-sum step per tick over a sorted bar array on algorithm-canvas; composed via `uses`.

std-astro-orbit.name: std-astro-orbit
std-astro-orbit.description: Kepler orbit simulator — the learner drags eccentricity and semi-major-axis sliders and steps the planet along its ellipse, watching equal-area sweeps confirm Kepler's second law, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-astro-stellar.name: std-astro-stellar
std-astro-stellar.description: Stellar life-cycle simulator — the learner picks a starting mass via slider or preset buttons and steps through the star's evolutionary stages from nebula to its predicted end state (white dwarf, neutron star, or black hole), on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-cell.name: std-bio-cell
std-bio-cell.description: Eukaryotic cell-structure engine — a large steady nucleus ringed by organelles whose radii breathe at staggered phases on biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-foodweb.name: std-bio-foodweb
std-bio-foodweb.description: Food-web / ecosystem engine — five trophic species whose radii breathe at staggered phases (trophic lag) on biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-mitosis.name: std-bio-mitosis
std-bio-mitosis.description: Cell-division engine — two daughter cells separate from and rejoin a shared center each mitosis cycle via a phase-driven triangle wave on biology-canvas.

std-bio-network.name: std-bio-network
std-bio-network.description: Generic declarative biology-network renderer — a fixed roster of nodes/edges/shapes (cells and organelles, food-web trophic links, or classification taxa) drawn once on a biology-canvas with no interaction or transitions. Node/edge/shape vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any static biology diagram. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-phasecycle.name: std-bio-phasecycle
std-bio-phasecycle.description: Staged biology phase-cycle engine — the learner steps a Next/Prev cursor through an ordered roster of stages (e.g. mitosis phases), each revealing its own node/edge/shape snapshot, label, and description, and can predict the next stage before revealing it for immediate correct/incorrect feedback. Stage vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any staged biology process, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-bio-population.name: std-bio-population
std-bio-population.description: Predator-prey population engine — Lotka-Volterra cycle via two out-of-phase oscillating node radii on biology-canvas.

std-bio-processrate.name: std-bio-processrate
std-bio-processrate.description: Photosynthesis-style process-rate engine — the learner adjusts light, CO₂, and temperature sliders and watches the process rate and its limiting factor recompute live, with input-node radii/colors on a biology-canvas reflecting each factor's saturation. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-branching-logic.name: std-branching-logic
std-branching-logic.description: std-branching-logic — survey skip-logic rules. Lists rules in `browsing`; opens rule detail in `viewing_single` with Edit / Delete actions.

std-chem-diffusion.name: std-chem-diffusion
std-chem-diffusion.description: Diffusion engine — two color-coded gases random-walk toward each other, mixing to illustrate entropy.

std-chem-molecule.name: std-chem-molecule
std-chem-molecule.description: Declarative molecule/reaction diagram — atoms, bonds, and arrows rendered on a chemistry-canvas with no learner-facing transitions. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-osmosis.name: std-chem-osmosis
std-chem-osmosis.description: Osmosis engine — water random-walks freely while trapped solute stays right of a semipermeable membrane, so water net-crosses toward the solute to equalize concentration.

std-chem-reaction.name: std-chem-reaction
std-chem-reaction.description: Reversible reaction engine — four A+B pairs oscillate together and apart, forming and breaking a bond on chemistry-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-chem-titration.name: std-chem-titration
std-chem-titration.description: Acid-base titration engine — the learner adds titrant in large or small increments and watches the pH curve and indicator color evolve toward (and past) the equivalence point, on a chemistry-canvas plus a pH line-chart. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-civics-billprocess.name: std-civics-billprocess
std-civics-billprocess.description: How a bill becomes law — a bill token travels Introduced -> House vote -> Senate vote -> President, with veto and a two-thirds congressional override, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-civics-checks.name: std-civics-checks
std-civics-checks.description: Checks-and-balances matrix — the learner names which branch of government can check a given governmental action, drawing the check arrow actor -> checker on a three-branch diagram, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-earth-plates.name: std-earth-plates
std-earth-plates.description: Plate-tectonics boundary simulator — the learner picks a convergent/divergent/transform boundary and advances motion to see landforms and earthquakes accumulate, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-earth-watercycle.name: std-earth-watercycle
std-earth-watercycle.description: Water-cycle flux simulator — the learner drives solar input and steps the cycle to watch evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and runoff fluxes rebalance across ocean, atmosphere, and land reservoirs, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-market.name: std-econ-market
std-econ-market.description: Supply-and-demand market engine — the learner shifts demand/supply curve intercepts and sets a price to see surplus or shortage emerge against the computed equilibrium, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-econ-ppf.name: std-econ-ppf
std-econ-ppf.description: Production-possibilities frontier engine — the learner drags an allocation slider dividing resources between two goods, reads the marginal opportunity cost, and toggles an idle-resources demo that drops actual output inside the frontier, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-koppen.name: std-geo-koppen
std-geo-koppen.description: Simplified Köppen climate classifier engine — the learner sets a summer/winter temperature and average-monthly-precipitation profile and a 12-month climograph classifies the climate by first-match-wins rule, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-geo-population.name: std-geo-population
std-geo-population.description: Age-sex population pyramid engine — the learner drives birth/death/migration rate dials and steps a five-cohort cohort-component projection, reading the dependency ratio and pyramid shape classification on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-hist-causalchain.name: std-hist-causalchain
std-hist-causalchain.description: WWI causal-chain counterfactual engine — the learner toggles structural causes and triggers off/on, a dependency cascade removes any cause whose enabling edge is gone, and the summed contribution of active causes is compared against a war threshold on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-classify.name: std-learn-classify
std-learn-classify.description: Generic classify-with-feedback instrument — items are presented one at a time, the learner picks a category from an ordered stacked-backdrop ladder, the pick is verdicted against the item's declared correct category with feedback and a running score, and the learner advances to the next item. Category and item vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any classification domain (needs hierarchies, checks-and-balances, sociological imagination, and beyond) on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-learn-stepper.name: std-learn-stepper
std-learn-stepper.description: Generic staged-sequence instrument — the learner moves a Next/Prev cursor across an ordered roster of stages, each revealing its label and description plus a running per-category tally, and can filter the timeline to a single category lens. Stage and category vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any ordered-sequence domain (periodization timelines, phase cycles, stellar evolution, and beyond) on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-soundchange.name: std-ling-soundchange
std-ling-soundchange.description: Historical sound-change stepper — the learner applies ordered Great Vowel Shift rules one at a time and watches every word whose vowel matches strike all at once, rendering the before/after pronunciation on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-ling-syntaxtree.name: std-ling-syntaxtree
std-ling-syntaxtree.description: Universal Grammar syntax-tree builder — the learner assembles a sentence's constituent structure bottom-up, attaching one labelled bracket (NP, VP, PP, S) at a time in derivation order, with evidence text on every pick and a growing bracket-tree render on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-inference.name: std-logic-inference
std-logic-inference.description: Propositional inference engine — the learner applies inference rules (modus ponens, modus tollens) step by step to derive new propositions from premises, building a guided proof toward a goal. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-logic-truthtable.name: std-logic-truthtable
std-logic-truthtable.description: Propositional truth-table engine — the learner toggles atomic proposition P/Q/R truth values and watches compound formulas (AND/OR/NOT/IMPLIES) re-evaluate live against every row of the truth table. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-math-linear.name: std-math-linear
std-math-linear.description: Linear-systems engine — line A's slope animates on a Cartesian plot; the two lines' intersection point slides with it.

std-math-numberline.name: std-math-numberline
std-math-numberline.description: Integer number-line engine — a marker hops integer-by-integer along y=0 on math-canvas, sweeping -9..9 via a phase-driven step.

std-math-sequence.name: std-math-sequence
std-math-sequence.description: Arithmetic-sequence engine — aₙ = a₀ + n·d plotted as dots on a straight line; a highlighted marker sweeps term-by-term on math-canvas.

std-math-sinewave.name: std-math-sinewave
std-math-sinewave.description: Sine wave — y = 5·sin(x − t); the whole waveform travels left as t advances (a real trig function plot).

std-math-unitcircle.name: std-math-unitcircle
std-math-unitcircle.description: Unit circle — a point sweeps the circle while its cos (horizontal) and sin (vertical) projections track on the Cartesian plot.

std-math-vectors.name: std-math-vectors
std-math-vectors.description: Vector addition engine — B oscillates via a triangle wave, animates the tip-to-tail A+B resultant on math-canvas.

std-physics-circular.name: std-physics-circular
std-physics-circular.description: Circular-motion engine — integrates bodies under a central force each tick and renders a physics-canvas via `uses`.

std-physics-collision.name: std-physics-collision
std-physics-collision.description: Elastic-collision engine — equal-mass circles exchange velocity along the collision normal and bounce off walls.

std-physics-diagram.name: std-physics-diagram
std-physics-diagram.description: Generic declarative physics-diagram renderer — a fixed roster of labeled points and shapes (field lines, ray paths, or circuit wiring) drawn once on a physics-canvas with no simulation tick. Shape/point vocabulary is entirely config-declared, so the same mechanism serves any static physics sketch. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-freefall.name: std-physics-freefall
std-physics-freefall.description: Free-fall engine — bodies drop under gravity, bounce off floor/walls losing energy; composed via `uses`.

std-physics-friction.name: std-physics-friction
std-physics-friction.description: Friction engine — decelerates sliding bodies via kinetic friction each tick and renders a physics-canvas.

std-physics-gas.name: std-physics-gas
std-physics-gas.description: Ideal-gas kinetic-theory engine — many equal-mass particles bounce elastically off walls and each other in a box.

std-physics-incline.name: std-physics-incline
std-physics-incline.description: Inclined-plane engine — slides a block down a frictional ramp under gravity via line-projection every tick and renders a physics-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`, controls auto-derived from @config.

std-physics-magnetic.name: std-physics-magnetic
std-physics-magnetic.description: Magnetic cyclotron engine — integrates charged bodies under F=qv×B each tick and renders a physics-canvas via `uses`.

std-physics-orbit.name: std-physics-orbit
std-physics-orbit.description: Orbital-motion engine — integrates bodies under inverse-square gravity toward a fixed central mass every tick and renders a physics-canvas via `uses`.

std-physics-pendulum.name: std-physics-pendulum
std-physics-pendulum.description: Pendulum engine — swings a bob about a fixed pivot via rigid-length projection, with Start/Pause/Reset controls; renders physics-canvas via uses. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-physics-projectile.name: std-physics-projectile
std-physics-projectile.description: Projectile-motion engine — integrates bodies under constant gravity with wall-bounce every tick and renders a physics-canvas; composed by a learning orbital via `uses`, controls auto-derived from @config.

std-physics-reflection.name: std-physics-reflection
std-physics-reflection.description: Reflection engine — photons travel straight, bouncing off box walls at equal angles; composed via `uses`.

std-physics-spring.name: std-physics-spring
std-physics-spring.description: Spring engine — Hooke's-law restoring force toward an anchor each tick; renders physics-canvas, composed via `uses`.

std-physics-wave.name: std-physics-wave
std-physics-wave.description: Wave engine — coupled oscillators where each interior point accelerates toward its neighbors' average height, with Start/Pause/Reset controls. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-bayes.name: std-prob-bayes
std-prob-bayes.description: Interactive Bayes' theorem engine — priors/likelihoods sliders drive a population-grid visualization (true/false positive/negative cells) and a computed posterior via Bayes' rule; a Run Evidence Trial button draws a random individual and accumulates an empirical posterior against the analytic one, on a math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-galton.name: std-prob-galton
std-prob-galton.description: Galton board engine — balls fall under gravity and random-walk past pegs, piling into a bell curve on a physics-canvas.

std-prob-montecarlo.name: std-prob-montecarlo
std-prob-montecarlo.description: Monte-Carlo π engine — ~250 points shimmer in a [-5,5] square; the red inside-circle fraction ≈ π/4 estimates π on math-canvas.

std-prob-trials.name: std-prob-trials
std-prob-trials.description: Declarative probability plotter — renders a distribution curve, sampled points, and extra shapes from config onto a math-canvas; no interaction beyond the initial render (dice-roll, coin-flip, and general distribution/histogram displays all share this mechanism — only the config data differs per topic). Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-prob-walk.name: std-prob-walk
std-prob-walk.description: Random-walk engine — a cloud of walkers starts at the origin and random-steps each tick into a widening Gaussian on math-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-psych-conditioning.name: std-psych-conditioning
std-psych-conditioning.description: Classical (Pavlovian) conditioning trial-runner — the learner runs CS+US pairing trials to drive an associative-strength curve toward its asymptote (acquisition), or runs CS-alone trials to drive it toward zero (extinction), via the Rescorla-Wagner rule plotted on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-imagination.name: std-soc-imagination
std-soc-imagination.description: Sociological Imagination engine — C. Wright Mills' exercise linking a personal trouble to the structural public issue behind it, with a drawn trouble→issue node map, per-link feedback and a running score, on a biology-canvas. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

std-soc-stratification.name: std-soc-stratification
std-soc-stratification.description: Social stratification & mobility engine — five class strata redistribute across generations as the learner drives an intergenerational mobility index, with a live Gini-index readout, on a biology-canvas stacked bar. Standalone by default; behind a lab router set matchMode and it renders only when MODE_SELECTED matches.

learning-astronomy-lab.name: learning-astronomy-lab
learning-astronomy-lab.description: Astronomy lab organism — a Kepler orbit simulator (drag eccentricity/semi-major axis, step the planet, watch equal-area sweeps) and a star life-cycle stepper (pick a starting mass, step from nebula to white dwarf / neutron star / black hole), composed from the std-astro-orbit and std-astro-stellar instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-biology-lab.name: learning-biology-lab
learning-biology-lab.description: Biology lab organism — a photosynthesis-style process-rate simulator (learner adjusts light/CO₂/temperature and watches the rate and limiting factor recompute), a mitosis phase-cycle stepper with predict-before-reveal, an animated breathing cell-structure diagram, an animated food-web ecosystem, and a declarative classification-network render, composed from the std-bio-processrate, std-bio-phasecycle, std-bio-cell, std-bio-foodweb, and std-bio-network instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-biology.name: learning-biology
learning-biology.description: Biology learning app — a fat organism whose orbitals are individual biology topics, each composed via `uses` from a per-topic engine atom on the biology-canvas.

learning-charts.name: learning-charts
learning-charts.description: Statistical charts organism — shows quantities, trends, proportions, and comparisons as bar, line, pie, area, donut, scatter, or histogram charts from labeled values or multi-series data.

learning-chemistry-lab.name: learning-chemistry-lab
learning-chemistry-lab.description: Chemistry lab organism — a declarative molecule diagram (atoms, bonds, and arrows on a chemistry-canvas), an animated reversible-reaction bond form/break oscillator, and an interactive acid-base titration simulator (pH curve, equivalence point, indicator color), composed from the std-chem-molecule, std-chem-reaction, and std-chem-titration instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-chemistry.description: Chemistry learning app — a fat organism whose orbitals are individual chemistry topics, each composed via `uses` from a per-topic engine atom on the chemistry-canvas.

learning-civics-lab.name: learning-civics-lab
learning-civics-lab.description: Civics lab organism — how a bill becomes law (a bill token travels Introduced -> House vote -> Senate vote -> President, with veto and a two-thirds override) and a checks-and-balances matrix (learner names which branch can check a given action, drawing the check arrow on a three-branch diagram), composed from the std-civics-billprocess and std-civics-checks instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-diagram.name: learning-diagram
learning-diagram.description: Semantic diagram organism — renders flowcharts, cycles, trees, and concept maps from typed nodes and edges; layout is computed deterministically by the renderer. Optional step-through stages highlight nodes one stage at a time.

learning-earth-lab.name: learning-earth-lab
learning-earth-lab.description: Earth-science lab organism — a plate-tectonics boundary simulator (learner picks convergent/divergent/transform and drives the motion) and an interactive water-cycle flux simulator (learner drives solar input and steps the cycle), composed from the std-earth-plates and std-earth-watercycle instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-economics-lab.name: learning-economics-lab
learning-economics-lab.description: Economics lab organism — a supply-and-demand market simulator (learner shifts demand/supply curves and sets a price to see surplus or shortage) and a production-possibilities frontier simulator (learner allocates resources between two goods and sees opportunity cost, with an inefficiency demo), composed from the std-econ-market and std-econ-ppf instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-geography-lab.name: learning-geography-lab
learning-geography-lab.description: Geography lab organism — an age-sex population pyramid simulator (learner drives birth/death/migration rate dials and steps a cohort-component projection across five age bands) and a simplified Köppen climate classifier (learner sets a summer/winter temperature and precipitation profile and a 12-month climograph classifies it), composed from the std-geo-population and std-geo-koppen instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-history-lab.name: learning-history-lab
learning-history-lab.description: History lab organism — a WWI causal-chain counterfactual (toggle structural causes and triggers off/on and watch whether war still breaks out) and a Fall-of-Rome periodization timeline (step through events and filter by political/military/economic lens), composed from the std-hist-causalchain and std-learn-stepper instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-linguistics-lab.name: learning-linguistics-lab
learning-linguistics-lab.description: Linguistics lab organism — a Universal Grammar syntax-tree builder (learner assembles a sentence's constituent structure bottom-up, one labelled bracket at a time) and a historical sound-change stepper (learner applies ordered Great Vowel Shift rules and watches every matching word's pronunciation shift at once), composed from the std-ling-syntaxtree and std-ling-soundchange instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-logic-lab.name: learning-logic-lab
learning-logic-lab.description: Propositional logic lab organism — toggle atomic proposition truth values and watch compound formulas evaluate live on a truth table, or apply inference rules (modus ponens, modus tollens) step by step to derive new propositions in a guided proof, composed from the std-logic-truthtable and std-logic-inference instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-math-lab.name: learning-math-lab
learning-math-lab.description: Math lab organism — plots functions, vectors, geometry, number lines, slope fields, and areas on a math-canvas.

learning-math.name: learning-math
learning-math.description: Math learning app — a fat organism whose orbitals are individual math topics, each composed via `uses` from a per-topic engine atom on the math-canvas.

learning-physics-lab.name: learning-physics-lab
learning-physics-lab.description: Physics lab organism — a rigid pendulum, a coupled-oscillator wave, and a shared declarative diagram atom rendering field/ray-diagram/circuit sketches, composed from the std-physics-pendulum, std-physics-wave, and std-physics-diagram instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-physics.name: learning-physics
learning-physics.description: Physics learning app — a fat organism whose orbitals are individual physics topics, each composed via `uses` from a per-law engine atom. kflow presents one orbital as one lesson.

learning-probability-lab.name: learning-probability-lab
learning-probability-lab.description: Probability lab organism — dice, coin-flip, and general distribution/histogram displays (all a declarative math-canvas plotter driven by config data), an animated random-walk display (converged onto the existing std-prob-walk tick-based integrator), and an interactive Bayes' theorem simulator with a population-grid visualization and evidence trials — composed from the std-prob-trials, std-prob-walk, and std-prob-bayes instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-probability.name: learning-probability
learning-probability.description: Probability learning app — a fat organism whose orbitals are individual probability topics, each composed via `uses` from a per-topic engine atom on the physics/math canvas.

learning-psychology-lab.name: learning-psychology-lab
learning-psychology-lab.description: Psychology lab organism — a classical (Pavlovian) conditioning trial-runner where the learner drives a Rescorla-Wagner acquisition/extinction curve, and a Maslow's-hierarchy-of-needs classifier where the learner sorts everyday scenarios onto a 5-tier needs pyramid, composed from the std-psych-conditioning and std-learn-classify instrument atoms behind a mode router.

learning-sociology-lab.name: learning-sociology-lab
learning-sociology-lab.description: Sociology lab organism — a social-stratification & mobility simulator (5 class strata redistribute across generations as the learner drives a mobility index) and a Sociological Imagination exercise (Mills: link each personal trouble to the public issue behind it), composed from the std-soc-stratification and std-soc-imagination instrument atoms behind a mode router.

std-marketing-article.description: Article section atom for marketing pages. Renders a centered prose block with title and rich content. Pick for about pages, mission statements, and blog-style content.

std-marketing-cta.name: std-marketing-cta
std-marketing-cta.description: Call-to-action banner atom for marketing pages. Renders a high-conversion CTA section with title, subtitle, and action buttons. Pick for conversion points at the end of pages or between sections.

std-marketing-features.name: std-marketing-features
std-marketing-features.description: Feature grid atom for marketing pages. Renders a responsive grid of feature cards with icons, titles, descriptions, and optional links. Pick for product capability showcases and benefit sections.

std-marketing-footer.name: std-marketing-footer
std-marketing-footer.description: Marketing footer atom for marketing pages. Renders a full footer with link columns, logo, and copyright. Pick for every marketing page bottom.

std-marketing-hero.name: std-marketing-hero
std-marketing-hero.description: Hero section atom for marketing pages. Renders a full-width hero with tag, title, subtitle, actions, and optional image. Pick for landing pages, product launches, and campaign microsites.

std-marketing-nav.name: std-marketing-nav
std-marketing-nav.description: Marketing navigation atom for marketing pages. Renders a sticky header with brand logo and nav links. Pick for site-wide navigation on static pages.

std-marketing-pricing.name: std-marketing-pricing
std-marketing-pricing.description: Pricing grid atom for marketing pages. Renders tiered pricing cards with plans, features, and CTAs. Pick for SaaS pricing pages and subscription showcases.

std-marketing-showcase.name: std-marketing-showcase
std-marketing-showcase.description: Showcase grid atom for marketing pages. Renders a grid of portfolio or product showcase cards with images, badges, and descriptions. Pick for product galleries and portfolio sections.

std-marketing-split.name: std-marketing-split
std-marketing-split.description: Split section atom for marketing pages. Renders a two-column layout with text and image alternating sides. Pick for feature deep-dives and alternating content sections.

std-marketing-stats.name: std-marketing-stats
std-marketing-stats.description: Stats grid atom for marketing pages. Renders a responsive grid of key metrics with values and labels. Pick for social proof, traction, and credibility sections.

std-marketing-steps.name: std-marketing-steps
std-marketing-steps.description: Step flow atom for marketing pages. Renders numbered steps horizontally or vertically. Pick for how-it-works sections and onboarding explainers.

std-marketing-team.name: std-marketing-team
std-marketing-team.description: Team grid atom for marketing pages. Renders a responsive grid of team member cards with avatars, names, roles, and bios. Pick for about pages and company culture sections.
